content:
Alice Nguyen: heads-up — observed a couple of hotplug races in prod today when we uploaded split safetensors checkpoints. model served briefly returned garbage shards until warmup finished. not a catastrophic outage but noisy :grimacing:
Ben Ortiz: ugh. which path triggered it? dedicated or hosted?
Alice Nguyen: hosted, small model bundle split into 12 shards. upload was async: we wrote shards in parallel and then uploaded a manifest. some workers started reading before manifest sync landed.
Carla M.: so manifestless reads + no per-shard checksum/ready flag = read-while-writing race. classic.
dev-bot: deploy-bot: new artifact "gpt-mini-v2-split" uploaded by @alice (12 shards) :package:  — integrity checks pending
Dan R: quick mitigation: atomic manifest flip. write to manifest.tmp then mv to manifest.json. workers only honor manifest.json.
Erin S: mv helps but doesn't solve mid-shard partial reads — if a shard file is uploaded and readable before fully flushed you can still get truncated reads. need per-shard ready marker or write to a staging dir then atomic rename into final dir.
Ben Ortiz: agree. propose this sequence: upload each shard to staging/<shard>.part -> fsync -> rename to shards/<shard>.safetensors -> once all present, write manifest.tmp -> fsync -> mv manifest.tmp -> manifest.json. workers only consult manifest.json and open final files.
Alice Nguyen: that sequence is fine for strongly consistent stores. but we also support remote object stores (S3/GCS) where rename isn't atomic. for S3, recommended pattern is upload shard then write manifest with content-lengths + checksums and a version token. workers validate checksums before activation.
Carla M.: checksum-validation on open is cheap compared to serving cost? we could sample-check first N bytes then verify in background. otherwise OOM/latency spikes for huge layers.
Dan R: we can do lazy-verify: open file, mmap first page and parse header, if header OK then accept shard into KV cache and enqueue full checksum job to background threadpool. on mismatch evict immediately and mark manifest version bad.
Erin S: +1. also suggest adding "activation lease" concept: manifest includes activation_token and activation_deadline. worker does atomic claim like `POST /catalog/claim?token=...` to mark it will activate; if claim fails, pick fallback model. helps with multiple controllers racing.
Ben Ortiz: the catalog claim can be implemented in our existing lease service (redis-backed), TTL small. if claimant dies, lease expires and next can try. handles in-cluster races.
Alice Nguyen: ergonomics: we should extend safetensors manifest schema to include per-shard checksum, bytes, compression flag, and optional staging_prefix. Minimal change to consumers: if manifest missing these fields fallback to old behavior but emit a warning.
Carla M.: backward compatibility is important. also add a small release toggle in runtime to enforce strict activation only for manifests >= v2.
Dan R: telemetry: emit metric `shard_activation_late` and `shard_checksum_mismatch`. will help quantify how often background verify finds issues.
Erin S: can we simulate uploads in CI by creating partial shard writes and ensuring runtime rejects them? a small fuzz test that truncates random bytes and checks behavior would be good.
Alice Nguyen: yes — I'll add a CI job to the weights-ingest pipeline. plan: implement staging upload + manifest v2 with checksums + lazy verify + claim/lease flow. follow-ups: API docs, runtime toggle, and a small migration plan for existing bundles.
Ben Ortiz: sounds solid. prioritize the manifest/lease pieces first. I can prototype the claim flow this week. :thumbsup:
Carla M.: I'll draft the manifest v2 schema and example.
dev-bot: ticket created: WGT-4321 "manifest v2 + staging/lease activation" assigned to @carla @ben @alice
Alice Nguyen: thanks — keep thread for implementation notes. if anyone sees a different corner-case ping me. :pray:
